summary: US EB-5 immigrant investor programme (1990-) and the executive-order Gold Card (2025-). Rules come from primary law (1990 Act, 1992 pilot, 2022 Reform and Integrity Act), Federal Register rules and court orders. Numbers come from official federal data: USCIS petition statistics (I-526/I-526E and I-829, FY1992-FY2026), DHS Yearbook counts of people who got permanent residence, State Department Visa Office tables, GAO reports and DHS rulemaking analyses. Federal data are good and consistent over time, though vintages and definitions differ (fee-paying vs all receipts; visas issued abroad vs adjustments). There are no official figures for the Gold Card's applications, approvals or money received.

sources.title: United States Citizenship and Immigration Services' Employment-Based Fifth Preference (EB-5) Regional Center Program (OIG-14-19)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Office of Inspector General
sources.covers: Audit of USCIS management of the EB-5 Regional Center Program: legal limits on terminating regional centers for fraud or national security, inability to show economic benefits, integrity problems; count of approved regional centers (Oct 2013); typical regional-center fees.
sources.notes: Official audit report addressed to USCIS Director Alejandro Mayorkas; USCIS concurred with three of four recommendations. Page numbers: PDF page, with printed page in brackets.

sources.title: Investigation into Employee Complaints about Management of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services' EB-5 Program
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Office of Inspector General
sources.author: John Roth
sources.covers: Investigation of whistleblower allegations that then-USCIS Director Alejandro Mayorkas intervened in three EB-5 matters (LA Films Regional Center, Las Vegas Regional Center, Gulf Coast Funds Management Regional Center); includes his written statement.
sources.notes: Memorandum from Inspector General John Roth to Secretary Jeh Johnson dated 24 March 2015 (date stamp on cover). Findings of an investigation, not a court decision; OIG says it could not determine his motives.

observations.location: PDF p. 68 (91 FR 40743), footnote 98
observations.quote: Between FY 2018 and 2022, USCIS terminated 388 regional centers.
observations.notes: DHS count from the USCIS list of terminated regional centers (last updated 1 Feb 2025). Includes terminations for not filing annual statements, which rose with the 2021-22 lapse and the 2022 Act.

observations.quote: DHS analysis of Form I–526 filing data for FY 2014–2016 indicates that on average, 13,103 Form I–526 petitions were filed annually.
observations.notes: Average per fiscal year of Form I-526 petitions filed, FY2014-FY2016.

observations.quote: Investments in regional centers accounted for an average of 12,042 such petitions annually, or 92 percent of all submitted Form I–526 petitions
observations.notes: Average per fiscal year, FY2014-FY2016.

observations.quote: non-regional center investments accounted for an average of 1,062 Form I–526 petitions annually, or about 8 percent.
observations.notes: Average per fiscal year, FY2014-FY2016.

observations.location: page header

observations.location: PDF p. 43 (printed p. 38)
observations.quote: USCIS reported that from program inception in fiscal year 1990 through fiscal year 2014, the EB-5 Program has created a minimum of 73,730 jobs and more than $11.2 billion in investments.
observations.notes: Not measured investment: USCIS multiplied the number of investors with approved I-526 petitions by USD 500,000. GAO found the method not valid or reliable (it can over- or understate). 'More than' USD 11.2 billion.

observations.location: PDF p. 25 (printed p. 20)
observations.quote: as of July 2015, SEC has initiated four civil enforcement actions alleging securities law violations by EB-5 Program participants.
observations.notes: SEC civil enforcement actions involving EB-5, cumulative, per an SEC official cited by GAO (Chicago Convention Center 2013, USA Now Regional Center 2013, Kansas Biofuel Regional Center 2014, Luca International 2015). Excludes administrative proceedings such as Ireeco (June 2015).

observations.location: PDF p. 25 (printed p. 20)

program_terms.applies_to: investor (spouse and children under 21 included); standard amount outside targeted employment areas

program_terms.notes: Statutory amount from the Immigration Act of 1990; investments counted from enactment, visas available from FY1992 (1 Oct 1991). The Act also allowed up to 3x more in high-employment areas, but DHS never set a higher amount (2019 rule, p. 5). Stayed in force until the 2019 rule took effect.

program_terms.applies_to: investor; targeted employment area (rural or at least 150% of national unemployment)

program_terms.notes: The 1990 Act let the government set a lower TEA amount of not less than half the standard (8 CFR 204.6(f), 1991 regulations, not stored). The USD 500,000 figure is printed in the USCIS table (usa-uscis-web-eb5-classification-2025) and GAO-15-696.

program_terms.notes: Applied to petitions filed from 21 Nov 2019. The rule was vacated on 22 June 2021 (Behring Regional Center LLC v. Wolf); USCIS then applied the pre-rule regulations, i.e. USD 1,000,000 / 500,000.

The Regional Center Program had lapsed from 1 July 2021, so only standalone investments could be filed from then until the 2022 Act.

events.title: Immigration Act of 1990 creates the EB-5 investor visa
events.description: Sec. 121 adds INA 203(b)(5) 'Employment creation': up to 10,000 visas a year for investors of USD 1,000,000 (as little as half in targeted employment areas) in a new enterprise creating 10 jobs, with 3,000 visas reserved for targeted employment areas, and two-year conditional residence (INA 216A). The new preference system took effect on 1 Oct 1991 (FY1992).
events.quote: Visas shall be made available, in a number not to exceed 10,000, to qualified immigrants seek- ing to enter the United States for the purpose of engaging in a new commercial enterprise

events.title: Congress creates the Regional Center (pilot) Program
events.description: Sec. 610 of the FY1993 Commerce-Justice-State appropriations act sets aside 300 EB-5 visas a year for five years for investors in regional centres, allowing jobs created indirectly to be counted. Later extended many times by appropriations acts.
events.quote: shall set aside 300 visas annually for five years

events.title: EB-5 Modernization rule raises minimum investment to USD 1.8 million / 900,000
events.description: DHS final rule published 24 Jul 2019, effective 21 Nov 2019: first increase since 1990 (CPI-U 1990-2015), five-yearly adjustment, DHS takes over high-unemployment TEA designation, priority-date retention. Vacated on 22 June 2021.
events.quote: This final rule is effective November 21, 2019.

events.title: Court vacates the 2019 EB-5 rule (Behring Regional Center v. Wolf)
events.description: The N.D. Cal. held that Acting DHS Secretary Kevin McAleenan was not lawfully serving when the rule was issued and vacated it; USCIS returned to the pre-2019 rules (USD 1,000,000 / 500,000).
events.quote: The Final Rule is VACATED and the matter is REMANDED to the Agency for further action.

events.title: Regional Center Program authorisation expires
events.description: The last short-term extension (Pub. L. 116-260, div. O, sec. 104) ran out on 30 June 2021. No new regional-center petitions could be approved until the 2022 Act; USCIS later resumed processing petitions filed on or before 30 June 2021. The lapse lasted until 15 March 2022 (program effective again 14 May 2022).
events.quote: Congress continuously extended the program, often through short-term extensions, until the last extension expired on June 30, 2021.

events.title: EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 signed
events.description: Division BB of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2022: minimum investment USD 1,050,000 / 800,000 (TEA and infrastructure), 32% of visas reserved (20% rural, 10% high unemployment, 2% infrastructure), automatic inflation adjustment from 2027, Regional Center Program reauthorised through 30 Sep 2027 with new integrity rules (Integrity Fund fees, audits, bona fides checks, promoter registration), repeal of sec. 610 of 1992.
events.quote: Visas under this subparagraph shall be made available through September 30, 2027

events.title: Reformed Regional Center Program takes effect
events.description: Sec. 103(b) of the 2022 Act took effect 60 days after enactment, i.e. on 14 May 2022, ending the lapse that began on 1 July 2021.
events.quote: effective May 14, 2022, through September 30, 2027.

events.title: Court bars USCIS from treating pre-2022 regional centers as deauthorised
events.description: In Behring Regional Center LLC v. Mayorkas the N.D. Cal. preliminarily enjoined USCIS's reading that the 2022 Act deauthorised all regional centers designated before it (over 600, per the court).
events.quote: The United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) interpreted the Act as unequivocally deauthorizing the 600-plus previously authorized regional centers.

events.title: USCIS starts collecting the EB-5 Integrity Fund fee
events.description: Annual USD 20,000 (or 10,000) fee per regional center under the 2022 Act; first payment window 2 March-3 April 2023, then each October.
events.quote: The first fee payment of the fees announced in this notice must be paid beginning on March 2, 2023 and before April 3, 2023.

events.title: USCIS fee rule raises EB-5 filing fees (I-526 to USD 11,160)
events.description: General USCIS fee rule effective 1 April 2024: I-526/I-526E from USD 3,675 to 11,160, I-829 from 3,750 to 9,525, regional center applications USD 47,695. Stayed for EB-5 forms on 12 Nov 2025.
events.quote: This final rule is effective April 1, 2024.

events.title: Executive Order 14351 creates the 'Gold Card' (decided)
events.description: The President ordered Commerce, State and DHS to set up within 90 days a Gold Card programme: a USD 1 million (individual) or USD 2 million (corporate) gift to the Department of Commerce counts as evidence for EB-1/EB-2 immigrant visas, with expedited processing; agencies to consider extending it to EB-5 investors. This is a binding executive order, but it creates no new visa category in law.
events.quote: I hereby announce the Gold Card, a visa program overseen by the Secretary of Commerce that will facilitate the entry of aliens who have demonstrated their ability and desire to advance the interests of the United States by voluntarily providing a significant financial gift to the Nation.

events.title: Gold Card order asks agencies to consider extending it to EB-5 (not decided)
events.description: Sec. 3(f) of EO 14351 directs agencies only to consider expanding the Gold Card to EB-5 applicants; no step to do so was found by 2 Oct 2026. The EB-5 programme itself continues under the 2022 Act.
events.quote: Consider expanding the Gold Card program to visa applicants under 8 U.S.C. 1153(b)(5).

events.title: DHS proposes a separate EB-5 fee rule (proposed)
events.description: Proposed rule to set EB-5 fees under sec. 106 of the 2022 Act and codify Integrity Fund fees; comments until 22 Dec 2025. Finalised 30 Sep 2026.
events.quote: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposes to adjust Employment-Based Immigration, Fifth Preference (EB–5) immigration benefit request fees

events.title: Court stays 2024 EB-5 fees (Moody v. Noem); USCIS reverts to old fees
events.description: The U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado held that the 2022 Act barred DHS from setting EB-5 fees in its general 2024 fee rule and stayed them; USCIS went back to the fees in force until 31 Mar 2024 the same day. The decision itself was not retrieved.
events.quote: On November 12, 2025, the United States District Court for the District of Colorado issued a decision in Moody v. Noem, 2025 WL 3157554 (D. Colo.), staying certain EB–5 related fees

events.title: USCIS publishes Form I-140G for Gold Card petitions
events.description: USCIS form page (last updated 10 Dec 2025; form edition 19 Nov 2025): petitioners first register and pay on trumpcard.gov, then file Form I-140G online; fee USD 15,000 per person. The exact date applications opened was not found in an official source.
events.location: sections 'Where to File' and 'When to File'
events.quote: You may only file Form I-140G after you have registered your information on trumpcard.gov and received confirmation your submission was accepted.

events.title: 'Trump Platinum Card' advertised as 'Coming Soon' (announced, not established)
events.description: trumpcard.gov invites foreign nationals to join a waitlist for a USD 5 million 'Trump Platinum Card' allowing up to 270 days a year in the US without US tax on non-US income. No executive order, regulation or law creating it was found; the tax treatment would need a legal basis. Date is when the page was seen, not when the announcement was first made.
events.quote: The Trump Platinum Card has not yet been released.

events.title: DHS proposes EB-5 integrity regulations (proposed)
events.description: Proposed rule implementing the 2022 Act's integrity provisions (regional center and project applications, audits, sanctions, automatic revocation of petitions, priority-date retention, bridge financing); comments closed 31 Aug 2026. Not final as of 2 Oct 2026.
events.quote: This proposed rule would implement the EB–5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 (RIA)

events.title: Cut-off date for protection of regional-center petitions if the program lapses
events.description: Under INA 203(b)(5)(S), added by sec. 108 of the 2022 Act, regional-center petitions filed on or before 30 Sep 2026 must continue to be processed and cannot be denied because the program expires (authorisation ends 30 Sep 2027).
events.quote: regional center that were filed on or before September 30, 2026

events.title: Final EB-5 fee rule: new fees from 30 Nov 2026
events.description: I-526 USD 7,615, I-526E USD 7,850, I-829 USD 5,000, I-956 USD 44,115; Integrity Fund fees up 10% (USD 22,000 / 11,000 per regional center, USD 1,100 per I-526E). Effective 30 Nov 2026.
events.quote: This final rule is effective November 30, 2026.

events.title: GAO finds EB-5 fraud risks poorly tracked and economic benefits unreliable
events.description: GAO-15-696: USCIS identified fraud risks (unlawful source of funds, investment schemes) but its systems could not support fraud analysis; its reported jobs and investment figures were not valid. SEC had brought four EB-5 civil enforcement actions by July 2015, including the Chicago Convention Center case (over USD 145 million raised from Chinese investors).
events.quote: were found liable for the fraudulent sale of over $145 million in securities to Chinese investors seeking a pathway to citizenship in the United States

events.title: SEC freezes assets in Chicago Convention Center EB-5 scheme
events.description: The SEC charged Anshoo R. Sethi, A Chicago Convention Center and Intercontinental Regional Center Trust of Chicago with selling more than $145 million in securities and collecting $11 million in administrative fees from over 250 mostly Chinese investors for a hotel and convention project, using falsified documents submitted to USCIS. Allegations at filing; an asset freeze preserved most of the money.
events.quote: fraudulently sold more than $145 million in securities and collected $11 million in administrative fees from more than 250 investors primarily from China

events.title: SEC and USCIS issue joint investor alert on EB-5 scams
events.description: Joint warning that USCIS designation of a regional center is not an endorsement of its investments, and that the SEC has taken emergency action against allegedly fraudulent EB-5 securities offerings.
events.quote: are jointly issuing this Investor Alert to warn individual investors about fraudulent investment scams that exploit the Immigrant Investor Program

events.title: DHS Inspector General finds USCIS cannot manage the Regional Center Program effectively
events.description: OIG-14-19: the law does not let USCIS deny or terminate regional centers on fraud or national-security grounds, USCIS cannot show economic benefits, and program integrity is weak (inconsistent application of rules, undocumented responses to outside inquiries).
events.quote: Several conditions prevent USCIS from administering and managing the EmploymentBased Fifth Preference regional center program effectively.

events.title: Inspector General: USCIS Director intervened in three EB-5 matters
events.description: The DHS OIG investigation, begun after a September 2012 whistleblower complaint, found that Alejandro Mayorkas, as USCIS Director, intervened outside the normal process in three EB-5 matters (LA Films, Las Vegas and Gulf Coast regional centers), creating an appearance of favoritism; OIG could not determine his motives.
events.location: PDF p. 3 [printed p. 1], Introduction and Summary
events.quote: In each of these three instances, but for Mr. Mayorkas’ intervention, the matter would have been decided differently.

events.title: SEC charges Jay Peak ski resort owners over EB-5 fraud
events.description: SEC fraud charges and asset freeze against Ariel Quiros, William Stenger, Jay Peak Inc. and related companies over more than $350 million raised from EB-5 investors for Vermont projects; the SEC alleged more than $200 million was used for other purposes, in Ponzi-like fashion. A receiver was appointed.
events.quote: raising more than $350 million from investors to construct ski resort facilities and a biomedical research facility in Vermont

events.title: Ex-wife of fugitive Chinese official pleads guilty to EB-5 visa fraud
events.description: Shilan Zhao pleaded guilty to conspiring to submit false documents (a false marriage certificate and documents on the source of the invested money) in an EB-5 application; her ex-husband, former Chinese official Jianjun Qiao, remained a fugitive. Plea was entered 9 January 2017; release dated 10 January.
events.quote: The indictment also accused them of lying about the source of Zhao's investment in the U.S.

events.title: Attorney pleads guilty in $50 million EB-5 fraud (California Investment Immigration Fund)
events.description: Victoria Chan admitted a scheme that collected more than $50 million from mainly Chinese investors through California Investment Immigration Fund, LLC, with about 130 fraudulent EB-5 applications; much of the money was stolen or refunded rather than invested.
events.quote: Chan admitted submitting about 130 fraudulent EB-5 visa applications to federal immigration authorities

events.title: Operators of New Orleans EB-5 Regional Center sentenced to 102 months
events.description: William B. Hungerford Jr. and Timothy O. Milbrath, convicted by a jury in September 2019 of defrauding investors while running the New Orleans EB-5 Regional Center after Hurricane Katrina, were each sentenced to 102 months. 31 immigrants had invested $15.5 million.
events.quote: A total of 31 immigrants invested a total of $15.5 million in the defendants’ investment fund.

events.title: Head of San Francisco Regional Center pleads guilty to EB-5 wire fraud conspiracy
events.description: Thomas Henderson admitted that the San Francisco Regional Center, which raised more than $100 million from foreign investors in 2011-2017, began using investor funds for other purposes by mid-2014; he also admitted a false statement to USCIS. Co-defendant Cooper Lee pleaded guilty to conspiracy.
events.quote: From 2011 to 2017, SFRC raised more than $100 million from foreign investors for seven commercial enterprises approved under the EB-5 program.

events.title: Jay Peak owner Ariel Quiros sentenced to five years for AnC Vermont EB-5 fraud
events.description: Quiros was sentenced to 60 months and ordered to pay $8,338,600.77 in restitution; co-defendants Stenger and Kelly got 18 months each and Choi remains at large. From 2012 to 2016 about 169 investors put about $85 million into the AnC Vermont biotech project, which was never built.
events.quote: From 2012 to 2016, the defendants convinced approximately 169 investors to invest approximately $85 million in the AnC Vermont project

programs.name: EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program (employment-based fifth preference, INA 203(b)(5)), including the Regional Center Program
programs.notes: Created by sec. 121 of the Immigration Act of 1990 (signed 29 Nov 1990; preference system in force from 1 Oct 1991, FY1992). Investors who invest the minimum in a new commercial enterprise creating 10 full-time jobs get two-year conditional permanent residence (green card) for themselves, spouse and children under 21, then file Form I-829 to remove conditions. Naturalisation is possible after five years of permanent residence (8 U.S.C. 1427). Regional Center Program added as a pilot in 1992 (sec. 610, Pub. L. 102-395), repeatedly extended, lapsed 1 July 2021-14 March 2022, reauthorised by the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 (Pub. L. 117-103, div. BB) in force from 14 May 2022 through 30 Sep 2027; regional-center petitions filed by 30 Sep 2026 are protected if the program lapses. Annual quota about 7.1% of employment-based visas (10,000 in the 1990 Act), with 20% rural, 10% high-unemployment and 2% infrastructure set-asides since 2022. First automatic inflation adjustment of the minimum investment due for petitions filed from 1 Jan 2027 (amount not yet published as of 2 Oct 2026). Run by USCIS (Immigrant Investor Program Office); visas allocated by the State Department.

programs.name: Gold Card programme ('Trump Gold Card'), Executive Order 14351
programs.notes: Established by Executive Order 14351 (19 Sep 2025), not by statute: an unrestricted gift to the Department of Commerce (USD 1 million for an individual, USD 2 million from a corporation for an employee) is treated as evidence for existing EB-1 (extraordinary ability) or EB-2 (exceptional ability / national-interest waiver) immigrant classifications, with expedited processing. Applicants register and pay on trumpcard.gov (Department of Commerce), then file Form I-140G online with USCIS (fee USD 15,000 per person); the gift is paid after vetting. Leads to ordinary permanent residence (not conditional), so naturalisation after five years under 8 U.S.C. 1427. The order asks agencies to consider extending it to EB-5. No official figures on applications, approvals or money received were found. The 'Trump Platinum Card' (USD 5 million) is only announced on trumpcard.gov ('Coming Soon'); no legal act creating it was found. Statutory basis and visa-number limits remain those of EB-1/EB-2.

new_indicators.name: Investment-pooling entities approved (stock)
new_indicators.definition: Number of intermediary entities authorised by the programme authority to pool investor money at a date (e.g. US EB-5 regional centers designated by USCIS).
new_indicators.notes: added by research:usa-eb5. Stock at a date.

new_indicators.name: Investment-pooling entities terminated
new_indicators.definition: Number of authorised intermediary entities (e.g. US EB-5 regional centers) whose designation was terminated by the programme authority in a period or cumulatively to a date, for any reason (non-filing of annual statements, fees, fraud, inactivity).
new_indicators.notes: added by research:usa-eb5. Say the cut-off and scope in notes.

new_indicators.name: Enforcement actions over investor-programme fraud
new_indicators.definition: Number of civil or criminal enforcement actions brought by an authority (e.g. US SEC civil actions, DOJ prosecutions) alleging fraud or securities violations connected with an investment-migration programme, cumulative to a date or in a period. Say which authority and whether administrative proceedings are included.

new_indicators.name: Open fraud investigations involving the programme
new_indicators.definition: Number of investigations by law-enforcement or programme integrity units concerning a residence- or citizenship-by-investment programme that are open at a date.
new_indicators.notes: added by research:usa-eb5. Stock at a date.

new_indicators.name: Petitions to remove residence conditions received
new_indicators.definition: Petitions filed by investors (e.g. US Form I-829) to remove the conditions on their conditional permanent residence, received in a period. The step after an initial investor petition and conditional residence; shows investors reaching the end of the conditional period.

new_indicators.name: Petitions to remove residence conditions approved
new_indicators.definition: Petitions to remove the conditions on an investor's conditional permanent residence (e.g. US Form I-829) approved in a period, regardless of when filed. Approval gives unconditional permanent residence.

new_indicators.name: Petitions to remove residence conditions denied
new_indicators.definition: Petitions to remove the conditions on an investor's conditional permanent residence (e.g. US Form I-829) denied in a period, regardless of when filed. Denial ends the conditional residence (subject to review in removal proceedings).

new_indicators.name: Petitions to remove residence conditions pending
new_indicators.definition: Petitions to remove the conditions on an investor's conditional permanent residence (e.g. US Form I-829) awaiting a decision at a date. A stock.
new_indicators.notes: added by research:usa-eb5. Stock at a date.

new_indicators.name: Approved investor petitions awaiting a visa number
new_indicators.definition: Approved investor immigrant petitions (e.g. US Forms I-526/I-526E) whose principal beneficiaries have not yet obtained permanent residence because no visa number is available under annual or per-country limits, at a date. Principal investors only, no family members.
new_indicators.notes: added by research:usa-eb5. Stock at a date; measures the visa backlog, not demand.

new_indicators.name: Immigrant visas issued abroad
new_indicators.definition: Immigrant visas issued by consular posts abroad under the programme's visa categories in a period, principal investors plus derivative spouses and children. Excludes adjustments of status by people already inside the country.
new_indicators.notes: US EB-5: State Department Report of the Visa Office, Table VI (Part IV), '5th Total'. Counted by foreign state of chargeability (normally country of birth).

new_indicators.name: Immigrant visa numbers used (visas issued plus adjustments of status)
new_indicators.definition: Immigrant visas issued abroad plus adjustments of status inside the country under the programme's categories in a period, i.e. numbers charged against the annual numerical limit; principal investors plus derivative spouses and children.
new_indicators.notes: US EB-5: State Department Report of the Visa Office, Table V (Part 3), '5th Total'. Counted by foreign state of chargeability (normally country of birth). The closest measure of people actually obtaining EB-5 green cards in a fiscal year (US fiscal year: 1 Oct-30 Sep).

new_indicators.name: Investor funds misused or misappropriated (per case)
new_indicators.definition: Amount that an authority (regulator, prosecutor or court) alleges or finds was misused, diverted or misappropriated from programme investors in a specific case, as stated by that authority
new_indicators.notes: Case-level, not a programme total. Notes must say whether the amount is an allegation (status claim) or adjudicated (court finding, plea, restitution order).

gaps: Gold Card: no official count of registrations, I-140G petitions, approvals or gifts received (USD) was found on uscis.gov, trumpcard.gov, commerce.gov or in the Federal Register. The only number is USCIS's PRA planning estimate of 1,520 self-petitioners and 72 corporate petitioners a year (91 FR 11559), which is not recorded as an observation.

Gold Card: the exact date applications opened (reportedly December 2025) is not in an official source we found. The USCIS I-140G page was last updated 10 Dec 2025. No Federal Register rule setting the USD 15,000 I-140G fee or the corporate 1%/5% fees was found. Lawsuits against the Gold Card were not searched (the web-search budget was used up).

Gold Card: the February 2025 presidential announcement of a USD 5 million 'gold card' replacing EB-5 was not recorded, because no official transcript was retrieved. The 'Trump Platinum Card' appears only as 'Coming Soon' on trumpcard.gov, with no legal act behind it.

Regional Center Program lapses before 2021 (e.g. during the Dec 2018-Jan 2019 government shutdown and other short gaps between appropriations extensions) are not documented here. The chain of extension acts from 1997 to 2020 (incl. Pub. L. 112-176 of 2012 and Pub. L. 116-260 div. O sec. 104) was not stored.
1991 implementing regulations (56 FR 60897, 29 Nov 1991; 8 CFR 204.6) that first set the USD 500,000 TEA amount were not stored. The 1991 start of the TEA amount comes from the 2019 rule's summary.
Moody v. Noem (D. Colo., 12 Nov 2025) staying the 2024 EB-5 fees: the court decision itself was not retrieved; it is recorded from DHS's account in the 2026 fee rule.
The 2027 inflation adjustment of the minimum investment (due for petitions filed from 1 Jan 2027) had not been published as of 2 Oct 2026.
No reauthorisation of the Regional Center Program beyond 30 Sep 2027 had been enacted as of 2 Oct 2026 (none found in the Federal Register; Congress.gov not checked, it blocks scripted access).
DHS integrity NPRM Tables 6 and 7 are images: their values were read by eye (Table 6 cross-checked by OCR), and the automatic quote check will not find them.
Older pre-2016 USCIS fee levels (I-526 USD 1,500, I-924 etc.) and the 2016 fee rule (81 FR 73292) were not recorded. Start dates of the USD 3,675 I-526 and USD 3,750 I-829 fees were not verified.
No USCIS file found with FY2013-FY2019 I-526 figures split into regional-center vs standalone investors; before FY2023 USCIS reports all I-526 petitions together.

FY2020 full-year I-526 and I-829 denials: the stored FY2020 Q4 all-forms PDF is cut off after the Approved column in the fiscal-year-to-date block (only quarterly denials are printed); not summed here.
From FY2023 USCIS gives no single EB-5 petition total; legacy I-526, standalone I-526 and I-526E are separate rows (breakdown form=...).

Country-of-birth figures for petitions exist only inside each set-aside category (I-526/I-526E receipt files FY2022-FY2026) and only for China, India, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and rest of world; no country totals across categories, so not recorded (one split per row). No country breakdown of approvals or denials was found.
No USCIS annual report to Congress on the EB-5 program (as required under the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022) was found on uscis.gov; the EB-5 resources page lists none.

No USCIS series for EB-5 investors or family members approved (persons), I-526 revocations, or regional center terminations by year (I-924/I-956 rows exist in all-forms reports but were not recorded).
FY1990-FY1991: the 1991-2013 file shows zero petitions in FY1991; no FY1990 data (program began with the Immigration Act of 1990, effective FY1992 for visas).

FY2025 Report of the Visa Office: no copy found. travel.state.gov blocks scripted downloads (HTTP 403) and the Wayback Machine has no capture of the FY2025 report page or any file under FY2025AnnualReport/ (CDX query returned nothing on 2026-10-02). The series therefore ends at FY2024.

Adjustments of status are not published separately by country for EB-5 in the Visa Office report: Table V combines visas issued and adjustments; Table VI has visas issued abroad only. The difference between the two could be computed but was not (no calculated numbers).
Before FY2005 not collected (reports for FY2000-FY2004 exist on the same page but use different table layouts; EB-5 numbers were small).

Visa-class breakdown (C5/T5/I5/R5 and the 2022 set-asides) recorded only for FY2022-FY2024 (after the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act); earlier years have C5/T5/R5/I5 columns too but were not split out.
Country breakdown is limited to the top eight countries of chargeability in each table (plus China, India and Vietnam always) and to values of 10 or more; other countries are in the stored tables.
FY2005 tables, FY2019 and FY2020 Table V are marked preliminary in the published files; no final revision was found, so those rows have status provisional.

No DHS OIG audit on EB-5 after OIG-14-19 (Dec 2013) appears in the OIG audits list (checked all pages, Oct 2026); none on the Gold Card. Special reviews/investigations other than the March 2015 Mayorkas report were not systematically searched.

No official SEC statement of the total number of EB-5-related enforcement actions was found; sec.gov blocks scripted access and the SEC EB-5 spotlight/enforcement pages, if any, were not located in the Wayback Machine. GAO-15-696 (parent) gives four actions as of July 2015.
Final outcomes of the SEC civil cases (Sethi/Chicago 2013, Jay Peak 2016: judgments, receivership recoveries) were not retrieved; amounts recorded are SEC allegations at filing.

DOJ press releases were found by title search of the justice.gov API only (keywords EB-5, EB5, immigrant investor); releases that do not name EB-5 in the title (e.g. the Sethi criminal case in N.D. Ill.) are missed.
No official programme-wide count of fraud cases, fraud referrals or EB-5 criminal convictions was found.
